name: Hairline tattoo
summary: Scalp micropigmentation tattoos tiny dots to mimic stubble or density along the hairline; sourcing is mostly industry and press, with no clinical trials found.
lead: A hairline tattoo, more formally scalp micropigmentation (SMP) or hair tattoo, is a non-surgical, superficial cosmetic tattoo that creates the look of closely shaved hair on a bald scalp or adds apparent density to thinning areas . It is also used to conceal hair transplant scars and other scars on the head .

name: Sulfate-free shampoo
summary: Shampoo made without SLS/SLES sulfates; marketed as gentler, with no trials on appearance outcomes.
lead: Sulfate-free shampoo is a shampoo formulated without the sulfate surfactants most common in conventional products, chiefly sodium lauryl sulfate (SLS) and sodium laureth sulfate (SLES). Instead it uses other cleansing agents such as sodium cocoyl glutamate or sodium cocoyl isethionate.

name: Co-washing
summary: Washing hair with conditioner instead of shampoo; gentle for dry or curly hair, with buildup the reported trade-off.
lead: Co-washing, short for conditioner washing, is the practice of cleansing hair with a conditioner or a dedicated cleansing conditioner instead of shampoo. It is mainly associated with dry, sensitive, chemically processed or textured and curly hair.

name: Olaplex bond builder
summary: Brand-defining bond-repair hair treatment; widely sold, but only company-cited testing and a lawsuit history in the sources.
lead: Olaplex is an American hair-care brand founded in 2014 whose products are marketed as repairing hair damaged by chemical, heat and mechanical stress. Its products contain a patented ingredient, bis-aminopropyl diglycol dimaleate, which the company says reconnects broken disulfide bonds in hair.

name: Keratin smoothing treatment
summary: Salon keratin-and-heat smoothing for frizz and curl; lasts months, with formaldehyde exposure the documented concern.
lead: A keratin smoothing treatment, also called a Brazilian keratin treatment or Brazilian blowout, is a salon procedure in which a keratin-based solution is applied to hair and sealed in with heat, with the aim of reducing frizz, adding shine and loosening curl. Results are described as semi-permanent, typically lasting a few months.

name: Perm / texture perm
summary: Chemical waving/curling of hair; established salon procedure, popular in forums as a PSL boost with no attractiveness research.
lead: A perm (permanent wave) is a chemical hairstyling procedure that reshapes hair into waves or curls by breaking and reforming the disulfide bonds in keratin. A reducing agent, classically ammonium thioglycolate, breaks the bonds while the hair is wrapped on rods, and a neutralizer such as hydrogen peroxide reforms them in the new shape.
claims: A perm boosts you by about "1 PSL".
A perm can compensate for weak eye-area features by covering them.

name: Hair relaxer / chemical straightener
summary: Alkaline chemical straightening of curly hair; effective cosmetically, with ongoing cancer and fibroid research and burn risks.
lead: A hair relaxer, or chemical straightener, is a cosmetic product that permanently loosens tight curls or straightens hair by breaking the bonds that hold its shape; new growth returns to its natural texture. Relaxers are almost always alkaline: lye relaxers use sodium hydroxide, and no-lye versions use other alkalis such as calcium, potassium or guanidine hydroxide, while others use thioglycolate or sulfite-based chemistry.

name: Hair botox / hair filler treatment
summary: A marketing name for protein-style smoothing treatments that promise less frizz and more shine; the term has no fixed formula and no direct trials.
lead: Hair botox, also marketed as a hair filler treatment, is the name given in the beauty industry to salon and at-home smoothing treatments that are described as depositing protein or conditioning agents on the hair to reduce frizz and add shine. The name borrows from injectable cosmetic procedures; it is a marketing term and has no single standard formulation.

name: Deep conditioner / hair mask
summary: A thicker, longer-contact conditioner for dry or damaged hair; it improves how hair feels and looks for now, but does not repair it.
lead: A deep conditioner, also called a hair mask, is a thicker and more concentrated version of hair conditioner, applied after washing and left on for a longer period than ordinary rinse-out conditioner before being rinsed off. Wikipedia describes typical contact times of about 20 to 30 minutes and says these products are aimed at very dry or damaged hair .

name: Leave-in conditioner
summary: A no-rinse conditioner for daily softness, slip and frizz control; the effects are cosmetic and temporary.
lead: A leave-in conditioner is a no-rinse hair product applied to damp (or sometimes dry) hair after washing and left in. It is sold for ongoing moisture, detangling, smoothing, frizz reduction and, in some formulas, heat protection . Formats include creams, lotions, sprays and mists .

name: Cold water rinse
summary: Finishing the wash with cold water, said to add shine by closing the cuticle; nobody has published a test of it.
lead: A cold water rinse is a hair-care habit of finishing a wash with cool or cold water. Proponents say it makes hair look shinier and smoother, with the reasoning that cold water closes or flattens the hair cuticle.

name: Apple cider vinegar rinse
summary: A diluted vinegar rinse after shampooing, said to clarify and add shine; supported only by anecdote, with burn and irritation reports for strong vinegar.
lead: An apple cider vinegar (ACV) rinse is a home hair treatment in which diluted apple cider vinegar is poured over the hair and scalp after washing. It is promoted as a clarifying rinse that removes product buildup, adds shine and smooths the cuticle.

name: Rice water rinse
summary: A starchy, often fermented rice soak used as a hair rinse; long tradition, thin research, and buildup reported on some hair types.
lead: A rice water rinse is a hair treatment in which the starchy liquid left from soaking, rinsing or boiling rice, often fermented for a day or two, is applied to the hair and scalp after shampooing. Proponents say it strengthens hair, reduces breakage and adds shine, and some say it helps hair grow longer .
claims: Fermented rice water makes hair grow longer.
Rice water strengthens hair and reduces breakage.

name: Egg hair mask
summary: A kitchen protein mask for hair; popular at home, with no trials behind it.
lead: An egg hair mask is a home hair-care treatment in which raw egg, or its white or yolk, is applied to the hair and scalp for a period before being rinsed out. It is promoted as a protein treatment for dry, damaged or weak-feeling hair, and is discussed in hair-care circles as a kitchen-ingredient alternative to commercial protein conditioners.

name: Castor oil
summary: A thick pressed seed oil people rub on hair, brows and lashes; established as a laxative, untested for growth.
lead: Castor oil is a thick, pale vegetable oil pressed from the seeds of the castor plant, Ricinus communis. About 90 percent of its fatty acids are ricinoleates . It has been used for centuries as a laxative and today also serves as an industrial raw material and cosmetic ingredient .
claims: Castor oil thickens brows and lengthens lashes.
Castor oil barely works compared with other options.
It is harmless even if the effect is unproven, since it coats hair like mascara.

name: Ayurvedic amla / bhringraj / shikakai
summary: Traditional Ayurvedic hair herbs; centuries of use, no clinical hair trials.
lead: Amla, bhringraj and shikakai are three plant materials from the Ayurvedic tradition of South Asia that are used in hair care, commonly as powders, pastes or infused oils. Amla is the fruit of Phyllanthus emblica (Indian gooseberry); bhringraj usually refers to Eclipta prostrata; shikakai is a pod-bearing plant used as a mild natural cleanser.

name: Satin bonnet / durag
summary: The silky head wrap that holds waves and protects hair overnight; a cultural staple with no clinical trials.
lead: A durag (also do-rag) is a close-fitting cloth head covering tied around the head to protect hair; a wave cap serves a similar purpose. Both originated in the African American community and are typically made of silk, satin, polyester or cotton . A satin bonnet is a related soft, smooth-lined cap, used for the same protective purpose.

name: 360 waves / wave brush
summary: Brush-and-durag training that coaxes coily hair into ripple patterns; cultural staple, no clinical research.
lead: Waves are a hairstyle for short, kinky or curly hair in which the curls are brushed or combed flat into a ripple-like pattern . '360 waves' refers to a pattern that encircles the whole head, and variants include 180, 540 and spin waves . The pattern is trained with a soft brush, moisturiser or pomade, and a durag or wave cap .

name: Hair texture powder / sea salt spray
summary: Salt mist and dry powder for matte, voluminous hair; cosmetic styling with no clinical research.
lead: Texture powders and sea salt sprays are hair styling products used to add volume, grip and a matte, tousled look. Sea salt spray is a salt-and-water mist applied to damp hair, while texture powder is a fine dry powder dusted at the roots.
claims: A homemade sea salt spray can make hair wavier or curlier.

name: Blow-dry and volumizing routine
summary: Drying hair upward with a dryer for temporary root lift; no trials, and the effect washes out.
lead: A blow-dry and volumizing routine is a hair-styling practice in which hair is dried with a handheld dryer, often while being lifted or directed upward at the roots, to give the hairstyle more height and body. It is discussed in looksmaxxing and grooming circles as a low-cost way to change the apparent fullness of the hair.

name: Heat protectant
summary: A pre-styling spray or serum sold to cushion hair from hot tools; untested in trials.
lead: Heat protectants are hair-styling products, sold as sprays, serums and leave-in treatments, that are marketed to reduce thermal damage from blow dryers, flat irons and curling irons. Descriptions say they coat the hair shaft with a film that slows heat transfer and limits moisture loss.

name: Diffuser curl drying
summary: A dryer attachment that spreads airflow to dry curls with less frizz; no trials, and the effect is temporary.
lead: Diffuser curl drying is the practice of drying hair with a hair-dryer attachment that spreads the airflow, usually to keep curls and waves defined while adding volume. It is discussed as a styling method for naturally curly, permed and fine hair.

name: Shower filter
summary: A chlorine-reducing filter for the shower arm; the skin and hair benefits are anecdotal.
lead: A shower filter is a point-of-use water filter fitted at the shower arm, either as an inline unit or as a showerhead with built-in media, intended to reduce contaminants in shower water, chiefly chlorine. Retail marketing frames them as a way to ease dry skin and brittle hair attributed to chlorinated or hard water.

name: Scalp exfoliation
summary: Scrubs and acids to clear scalp flakes and buildup; some flaking data, no hair-growth trials.
lead: Scalp exfoliation is a hair-care practice that uses physical scrubs, chemical exfoliants such as salicylic or glycolic acid, or hybrids to remove dead skin cells, oil and product buildup from the scalp. Proponents say it reduces flaking, helps products absorb and supports hair growth.

name: Protein intake for hair
summary: Eating enough protein for hair; deficiency links are noted, but no trials test extra protein.
lead: Protein intake for hair is the idea that eating enough protein supports hair growth and quality, because hair is made largely of keratin. It is discussed in lifestyle sections of hair and looksmaxxing communities.

name: Gelatin / bone broth
summary: Collagen-rich foods that fans tie to skin and hair; the published record on appearance benefits is essentially empty.
lead: Gelatin and bone broth are collagen-derived foods. Gelatin is made by partially breaking down animal collagen, mostly from pork skin, bones and cattle hides, and gels in water . Bone broth is a long-simmered stock of animal bones and connective tissue, in which collagen converts to gelatin and thickens the liquid .

name: Brushing technique (boar bristle)
summary: Natural-bristle brushing for smoothness and shine; the oil-distribution claim has no published tests behind it.
lead: Boar bristle brushing means using a brush with natural boar hair bristles to smooth and style hair. Such brushes are described as having tightly spaced bristles that increase tension while brushing in order to smooth the hair .

name: Haircut for face shape
summary: Picking a cut by face proportions: a popular styling rule of thumb with no published tests behind it.
lead: Choosing a haircut for face shape is the practice of selecting a style to suit the proportions of the face, such as oval, round or square. Advocates in styling and looksmaxxing circles say particular cuts can balance or flatter particular facial proportions.

name: Middle part / curtains / textured crop trends
summary: Middle parts, curtains and textured crops: trending cuts with a long history and no studies on their effect on attractiveness.
lead: Curtains is a hairstyle with a long fringe divided by a middle or side parting, usually with shorter sides and back . In recent years it has been associated with K-pop artists, and middle parts and textured crops are discussed as current men's cuts.

name: Gray hair reversal supplements
summary: Copper, B12 and similar pills marketed for restoring hair color; reversal is reported only where a deficiency caused the greying.
lead: Gray hair reversal supplements are products and nutrients, such as copper and vitamin B12, that some people take hoping to restore natural hair color. Gray hair has no gray pigment; it results from reduced melanin production at the root .
